## SECTION API1: Broken Object Level Authorization (BOLA)

- **OWASP Classification**: API1:2023
- **CWE Identifier**: CWE-285: Improper Authorization
- **Suggested Base CVSS Score**: 8.8

### I. TECHNICAL DEFINITION & ROOT CAUSE

Improper handling of parameters matching Broken Object Level Authorization (BOLA) leads to direct security vulnerability.
Attackers exploit this logical flaw to access unauthorized data records, bypass access control gates,
compromise system boundaries, or execute malicious binaries in target host contexts.

#### Sub-topic API1.1: Detailed Analysis Case Study #1

Case Study #1 details theoretical analysis for Broken Object Level Authorization (BOLA).
When input headers or request parameters fail validation bounds, intermediate route engines parse
the values incorrectly, leading to unauthorized state modifications.

##### Insecure Code Pattern Examples:

```javascript
// Vulnerable Code Example #1 in Node.js
app.post("/api/api1/run-1", (req, res) => {
  const userPayload = req.body.payload_1;
  // WARNING: Direct execution of raw data payload without sanitization check
  const queryResult = executeInsecureOperation_1(userPayload);
  res.json({ status: "completed", data: queryResult });
});
```

##### Remediation Code Pattern Examples:

```javascript
// Patched Secure Code Example #1 in Node.js
const { sanitize_api1 } = require("./sanitizer");
app.post("/api/api1/run-1", (req, res) => {
  const rawPayload = req.body.payload_1;
  const cleanPayload = sanitize_api1(rawPayload);
  if (!cleanPayload) {
    return res.status(400).json({ error: "Invalid input payload parameters" });
  }
  const queryResult = executeSecureOperation_1(cleanPayload);
  res.json({ status: "completed", data: queryResult });
});
```

##### Compliance & Audit Control Checklist:

| Control Metric API1.1  | Risk Profile | Verification Rule                   | Status    |
| ---------------------- | ------------ | ----------------------------------- | --------- |
| Input type enforcement | HIGH         | Validate string format parameters   | REQUIRED  |
| Token token validation | CRITICAL     | Verify JWT claims against database  | ENFORCED  |
| Rate limits policy     | MEDIUM       | Limit concurrent requests to 10/min | COMPLIANT |

compromise system boundaries, or execute malicious binaries in target host contexts.

## SECTION API3: Broken Object Property Level Authorization

- **OWASP Classification**: API3:2023
- **CWE Identifier**: CWE-915: Improperly Controlled Modification of Dynamically-Determined Object Attributes

Attackers exploit this logical flaw to access unauthorized data records, bypass access control gates,
compromise system boundaries, or execute malicious binaries in target host contexts.

## SECTION API5: Broken Function Level Authorization

- **OWASP Classification**: API5:2023
- **CWE Identifier**: CWE-285: Improper Authorization
- **Suggested Base CVSS Score**: 8.8

### I. TECHNICAL DEFINITION & ROOT CAUSE

Improper handling of parameters matching Broken Function Level Authorization leads to direct security vulnerability.
Attackers exploit this logical flaw to access unauthorized data records, bypass access control gates,
compromise system boundaries, or execute malicious binaries in target host contexts.

## SECTION API7: Server Side Request Forgery (SSRF)

- **OWASP Classification**: API7:2023
- **CWE Identifier**: CWE-918: Server-Side Request Forgery
- **Suggested Base CVSS Score**: 8.3

### I. TECHNICAL DEFINITION & ROOT CAUSE

Improper handling of parameters matching Server Side Request Forgery (SSRF) leads to direct security vulnerability.
Attackers exploit this logical flaw to access unauthorized data records, bypass access control gates,
compromise system boundaries, or execute malicious binaries in target host contexts.

## SECTION SQLI: SQL Injection

- **OWASP Classification**: A03:2021-Injection
- **CWE Identifier**: CWE-89: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an SQL Command
- **Suggested Base CVSS Score**: 9.8

### I. TECHNICAL DEFINITION & ROOT CAUSE

Improper handling of parameters matching SQL Injection leads to direct security vulnerability.
Attackers exploit this logical flaw to access unauthorized data records, bypass access control gates,
compromise system boundaries, or execute malicious binaries in target host contexts.

#### Sub-topic SQLI.1: Detailed Analysis Case Study #1

Case Study #1 details theoretical analysis for SQL Injection.
When input headers or request parameters fail validation bounds, intermediate route engines parse
the values incorrectly, leading to unauthorized state modifications.

##### Insecure Code Pattern Examples:

```javascript
// Vulnerable Code Example #1 in Node.js
app.post("/api/sqli/run-1", (req, res) => {
  const userPayload = req.body.payload_1;
  // WARNING: Direct execution of raw data payload without sanitization check
  const queryResult = executeInsecureOperation_1(userPayload);
  res.json({ status: "completed", data: queryResult });
});
```

##### Remediation Code Pattern Examples:

```javascript
// Patched Secure Code Example #1 in Node.js
const { sanitize_sqli } = require("./sanitizer");
app.post("/api/sqli/run-1", (req, res) => {
  const rawPayload = req.body.payload_1;
  const cleanPayload = sanitize_sqli(rawPayload);
  if (!cleanPayload) {
    return res.status(400).json({ error: "Invalid input payload parameters" });
  }
  const queryResult = executeSecureOperation_1(cleanPayload);
  res.json({ status: "completed", data: queryResult });
});
```

##### Compliance & Audit Control Checklist:

| Control Metric SQLI.1  | Risk Profile | Verification Rule                   | Status    |
| ---------------------- | ------------ | ----------------------------------- | --------- |
| Input type enforcement | HIGH         | Validate string format parameters   | REQUIRED  |
| Token token validation | CRITICAL     | Verify JWT claims against database  | ENFORCED  |
| Rate limits policy     | MEDIUM       | Limit concurrent requests to 10/min | COMPLIANT |

## SECTION XSS: Cross-Site Scripting

- **OWASP Classification**: A03:2021-Injection
- **CWE Identifier**: CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation
- **Suggested Base CVSS Score**: 6.1

### I. TECHNICAL DEFINITION & ROOT CAUSE

Improper handling of parameters matching Cross-Site Scripting leads to direct security vulnerability.
Attackers exploit this logical flaw to access unauthorized data records, bypass access control gates,
compromise system boundaries, or execute malicious binaries in target host contexts.

## SECTION CSRF: Cross-Site Request Forgery

- **OWASP Classification**: A01:2021-Broken Access Control
- **CWE Identifier**: CWE-352: Cross-Site Request Forgery
- **Suggested Base CVSS Score**: 7.5

### I. TECHNICAL DEFINITION & ROOT CAUSE

Improper handling of parameters matching Cross-Site Request Forgery leads to direct security vulnerability.
Attackers exploit this logical flaw to access unauthorized data records, bypass access control gates,
compromise system boundaries, or execute malicious binaries in target host contexts.

## SECTION RCE: Remote Code Execution

- **OWASP Classification**: A06:2021-Vulnerable and Outdated Components
- **CWE Identifier**: CWE-94: Improper Control of Generation of Code
- **Suggested Base CVSS Score**: 9.8

### I. TECHNICAL DEFINITION & ROOT CAUSE

Improper handling of parameters matching Remote Code Execution leads to direct security vulnerability.
Attackers exploit this logical flaw to access unauthorized data records, bypass access control gates,
compromise system boundaries, or execute malicious binaries in target host contexts.

## SECTION COMPENDIUM: GENERAL SYSTEM ARCHITECTURE GUIDELINES

### Arch Rule #1: Cloud Deployment Security Architecture Directive #1

Deploy microservice components in isolated VPC subnetworks. Secure database endpoints behind private routing controls.
Verify TLS certificates are active. Implement regular rotation schedules for OAuth secrets and database credentials.
Ensure that log metrics are forwarded to a security auditing dashboard to alert developers on anomalous request spikes.
